differences.title: 1. ISOLATION LEVEL
differences.leftDesc: WebAssembly runs in a restricted sandbox, offering fine-grained memory safety and preventing direct OS access, ensuring predictable execution.
differences.rightDesc: Containers virtualize the OS kernel, providing process and filesystem isolation, but share the host OS kernel, posing potential security risks.

differences.title: 2. STARTUP TIME
differences.leftDesc: Wasm modules compile and execute extremely quickly, often within milliseconds, due to their lightweight design and lack of OS overhead.
differences.rightDesc: Container startup involves booting a full OS environment or a complex init process, leading to significantly longer startup times.

differences.title: 3. SIZE & FOOTPRINT
differences.leftDesc: Wasm binaries are exceptionally small, typically kilobytes, making them ideal for edge computing, embedded systems, and rapid deployment.
differences.rightDesc: Container images include an entire OS filesystem and libraries, resulting in large sizes often measured in megabytes or gigabytes.

differences.title: 4. PORTABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Wasm code runs consistently across different operating systems and hardware architectures via a standardized virtual machine, ensuring true portability.
differences.rightDesc: Containers are tied to the host OS kernel architecture; a Linux container won't run natively on Windows or macOS without emulation.

differences.title: 5. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Wasm's ahead-of-time compilation and efficient virtual instruction set achieve performance close to native code, often surpassing interpreted languages.
differences.rightDesc: Containers introduce virtualization overhead. Performance can be excellent but is generally less predictable and slightly slower than direct native execution.

differences.title: 6. SECURITY MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Wasm enforces security via explicit capabilities granted at runtime, preventing unauthorized access to system resources by design.
differences.rightDesc: Containers rely on kernel features like namespaces and cgroups for isolation, which can have complex security implications and require careful configuration.

differences.title: 7. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for client-side web apps, serverless functions, plugins for existing applications, and secure code execution on untrusted input.
differences.rightDesc: Perfect for packaging and deploying complex applications, microservices architectures, and ensuring consistent environments from development to production.
